scenario: AITA for telling an intern to throw her banana peel in the trash? | A few details to set the stage: To get into my place of work, one needs to walk from the parking lot down a sidewalk that is along the side of the building. The other side of the sidewalk is semi-wooded with low growing evergreen shrubs. This sidewalk is about 100ft long, and has a trash can at either end. Also, in the last month, there have been a ton of flies buzzing around this area, so much so that the building manager called an exterminator. This morning, I (\~30s F) witnessed an intern (20s F) for one of the companies in our building walking into work eating a banana. About 3/4 of the way down the sidewalk, with a trashcan not even 25 feet away, she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. It landed on top of the bush and she just kept walking. I wasn't sufficiently caffeinated to be polite, so I blurted out "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" complete with the WTF hand gesture; pointing to the trash can. She ripped into me, claiming it's organic and feeds the animals. She was half yelling / half crying. I pointed at the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to "pick up your (her) damn banana peel." Instead she cried loudly saying something unintelligible, got her peel, and put it in the trash. I'm thinking, great, this is over. Maybe she won't toss her banana debris into the bushes and we will have less flies. I'm sure I could have been more nice about it / sworn less, but I was just so shocked to see someone litter like that. I badged in to the building and she walked in behind me. At some point, she must have cried to her boss about it, because her boss found me today and asked if I confronted her intern. I said I had, then explained, as I have done here, about the banana peel. I guess she spent all morning crying about how "mean" I was and couldn't do any work. My brain was screaming "drama queen" but I apologized instead for upsetting the intern. We laughed together about absurdity of it all, especially over a banana peel! But now that it's the weekend and I'm sufficiently caffeinated, I'm wondering AITA for calling her out?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by telling the intern to throw her banana peel in the trash. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, the setting: I work in a building where you have to walk from the parking lot down a 100-foot-long sidewalk to get to the entrance. On one side of this sidewalk, there are low-growing evergreen shrubs, and on the other side, there are trash cans at both ends. Recently, there have been a lot of flies buzzing around the area, so much so that the building manager had to call an exterminator. This morning, I saw an intern from one of the companies in the building walking in while eating a banana. She was about three-quarters of the way down the sidewalk when she tossed the banana peel into the bushes. At that point, the nearest trash can was only about 25 feet away. I was a bit upset because I wasn't caffeinated enough to be polite, so I blurted out, "What the hell? There's a trash can right in front of you!" with a hand gesture. The intern got defensive, claiming that the banana peel is organic and feeds the animals. She was half-yelling and half-crying. I pointed out the peel sitting on top of the bush and told her to pick it up. Instead, she cried loudly, got the peel, and threw it in the trash. I thought that was the end of it, hoping she wouldn't litter again and that we'd have fewer flies. Later, her boss approached me and asked if I had confronted her intern. I explained the situation, and I think she spent the whole morning crying about how mean I was and couldn't do any work. My initial thought was that she was being dramatic, but I apologized for upsetting her. We both laughed about how absurd the situation was, especially over a banana peel. Now, on the weekend, I'm wondering if I overreacted. Was it appropriate for me to call her out like that? Okay, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things: 1. **The Impact of Littering**: Throwing banana peels into bushes might seem harmless, but it can attract flies and other pests, which was already an issue in the building. So, from a practical standpoint, it's better to dispose of waste properly to maintain cleanliness and hygiene. 2. **Workplace Etiquette**: As an employee, especially someone in a supervisory role, it's important to set a good example and encourage others to follow workplace rules. However, the way I confronted her was abrupt and not very kind. 3. **Communication Style**: I was not at my best because I wasn't caffeinated, which led me to react impulsively. A more calm and respectful approach would have been better, especially since the intern was new and possibly sensitive to criticism. 4. **Consequences of My Action**: The intern was upset enough to cry and tell her boss, which led to an uncomfortable situation for both of us. While I apologized, it's clear that my approach had a negative impact on her workday. 5. **Alternative Approaches**: Instead of confronting her in an angry manner, I could have gently reminded her about the importance of using the trash cans to keep the area clean and pest-free. 6. **Personal Reflection**: It's important to reflect on how my actions affect others, especially in a professional setting. While I had good intentions to maintain cleanliness, my method of addressing the issue was not ideal. 7. **Learning Opportunity**: This situation serves as a reminder to approach such incidents with patience and kindness, even when I'm upset or not at my best. So, considering all these points, I think my initial reaction was not the best way to handle the situation. While the intent was good, the manner in which I addressed it was harsh and led to unnecessary emotional distress for the intern. It would have been better to handle it more calmly and respectfully, ensuring that the message was conveyed without making the other person feel attacked. In conclusion, while it's important to address littering to maintain a clean environment, the way I did it was not appropriate. I should have taken a more considerate approach to communicate my concerns effectively without causing offense or emotional upset.
